name: MathlibAnnex.DeterminantFrame.inverseBoundConstant_bound
title: A common inverse estimate from row Cramer

content.display_title: A common inverse estimate from row Cramer
content.one_sentence_role: Controls all near-maximal inverse frames by an explicit basis-dependent constant.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real normed vector space, and fix an ordered basis $b=(b_j)_{j=1}^n$. Write $C_b:E\to\mathbb R^n$ for the coordinate isomorphism, defined by $x=\sum_{j=1}^n(C_bx)_j b_j$, and give its coordinate space the sup norm $\|c\|_\infty=\max_j|c_j|$ (zero in dimension zero). A frame is an ordered family $F=(\ell_i)_{i=1}^n$ of continuous real linear functionals, with no independence assumed. Its matrix and evaluation map are
$$M_F=(\ell_i(b_j))_{i,j},\qquad T_Fx=(\ell_i(x))_i=M_FC_bx.$$
The admissible frames form the product of closed dual unit balls
$$\mathcal U=\{F:\|\ell_i\|_{E^*}\le1\text{ for every }i\}.$$
The norm on $E$ need not be a coordinate sup norm. Let $e_i^*(x)=(C_bx)_i$ be the dual coordinate functionals, and put $D_b=\max_{F\in\mathcal U}|\det M_F|$ and $\alpha_b=(1+\sum_i\|e_i^*\|_{E^*})^{-1}$. Fix $\eta<D_b$. Define
$$A_b(\eta)=\frac{nD_b}{\alpha_b(D_b-\eta)},\qquad
K_b(\eta)=1+\|C_b^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}A_b(\eta).$$
For $F\in\mathcal N_{b,\eta}=\{F\in\mathcal U:D_b-\eta\le|\det M_F|\}$ and every $c\in\mathbb R^n$,
$$\|C_b^{-1}(M_F^{-1}c)\|_E\le K_b(\eta)\|c\|_\infty.$$
content.assumptions: The only deficit hypothesis is $\eta<D_b$; the frame satisfies both the dual-row contraction condition and the displayed determinant lower bound. The coefficient $c$ is arbitrary. There is no extra $\eta\ge0$ hypothesis.
content.conclusion: The same positive $K_b(\eta)$ works for every frame in this near-maximal set and every coefficient. The coordinate inverse $C_b^{-1}$ and matrix inverse $M_F^{-1}$ are distinct maps; the resulting norm is the given norm of $E$.
content.proof_summary: Use row Cramer with a scaled coordinate functional, divide by the determinant gap, and transport the coordinate bound through the inverse coordinate map.

proof_steps.text:
**Read the row-Cramer identity one coordinate at a time.** Since $F\in\mathcal N_{b,\eta}$ and $\eta<D_b$,
   $$|\det M_F|\ge D_b-\eta>0.$$
   For $r\in E^*$, let $M_F[i\leftarrow r]$ denote the matrix obtained by replacing row $i$ with $(r(b_k))_{k=1}^n$. The row-Cramer formula is
   $$\det M_F[i\leftarrow r]
   =(\det M_F)\sum_{k=1}^n r(b_k)(M_F^{-1})_{ki}.$$
   Here $i$ specifies the replaced row, while $k$ runs over the basis coordinates. Apply [provider row form of Cramer](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/360da6fa66c1273b76b6b2d8c5666fd5ac2e3b56/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/NonsingularInverse.lean#L661-L666) to $M_F$ and the row $(r(b_k))_k$; its determinant hypothesis is the nonvanishing just shown. The provider uses $M_F^{\mathsf T}$, so its column replacement is exactly the row replacement above.

**Multiply by the coefficients and show the two sums.** For the same functional $r$ and the given column $c$,
   $$\begin{aligned}
   \sum_{i=1}^n c_i\det M_F[i\leftarrow r]
   &=(\det M_F)\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{k=1}^n c_i r(b_k)(M_F^{-1})_{ki}\\
   &=(\det M_F)\sum_{k=1}^n r(b_k)\left(\sum_{i=1}^n(M_F^{-1})_{ki}c_i\right)\\
   &=(\det M_F)\sum_{k=1}^n r(b_k)(M_F^{-1}c)_k.
   \end{aligned}$$
   The second line interchanges two finite sums; the third is matrix multiplication. Finally, linearity of $r$ and the definition of $C_b^{-1}$ give
   $$\begin{aligned}
   \sum_{k=1}^n r(b_k)(M_F^{-1}c)_k
   &=r\left(\sum_{k=1}^n(M_F^{-1}c)_k b_k\right)\\
   &=r\bigl(C_b^{-1}(M_F^{-1}c)\bigr).
   \end{aligned}$$
   Thus these calculations give [the row-replacement identity in basis coordinates](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L328-L367), with this same $F,r,c$. The column $M_F^{-1}c$ is a coordinate vector; only $C_b^{-1}(M_F^{-1}c)$ is the corresponding vector of $E$.

**Select one coordinate and bound its numerator.** Fix $j$ and take $r=\alpha_b e_j^*$. The definition of $\alpha_b$ gives
   $$\|\alpha_b e_j^*\|_{E^*}
   =\frac{\|e_j^*\|_{E^*}}{1+\sum_k\|e_k^*\|_{E^*}}\le1.$$
   This is [scaled-row admissibility](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L217-L229). Hence replacing any row $i$ of the admissible frame $F$ with this $r$ gives another admissible frame, by [admissible row replacement](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L445-L454), and [the determinant maximum](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L456-L464) gives
   $$|\det M_F[i\leftarrow\alpha_b e_j^*]|\le D_b\qquad(1\le i\le n).$$
   In Step 2 the functional evaluation is now exactly
   $$(\alpha_b e_j^*)\bigl(C_b^{-1}(M_F^{-1}c)\bigr)=\alpha_b(M_F^{-1}c)_j.$$
   Taking absolute values in that identity and bounding each summand yields
   $$\begin{aligned}
   \alpha_b|\det M_F|\,|(M_F^{-1}c)_j|
   &=\left|\sum_i c_i\det M_F[i\leftarrow\alpha_b e_j^*]\right|\\
   &\le\sum_i |c_i|\,|\det M_F[i\leftarrow\alpha_b e_j^*]|\\
   &\le\sum_i\|c\|_\infty D_b
    =nD_b\|c\|_\infty.
   \end{aligned}$$
   This is [the Cramer numerator bound](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L466-L485) for the same frame, coefficient column and scaled coordinate functional.

**Divide by the gap and return to the given norm.** Since $\alpha_b>0$ and $|\det M_F|\ge D_b-\eta>0$, the previous estimate implies
   $$\begin{aligned}
   \alpha_b(D_b-\eta)|(M_F^{-1}c)_j|&\le nD_b\|c\|_\infty,\\
   |(M_F^{-1}c)_j|
   &\le\frac{nD_b}{\alpha_b(D_b-\eta)}\|c\|_\infty
    =A_b(\eta)\|c\|_\infty.
   \end{aligned}$$
   This is the [coordinatewise inverse estimate](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L487-L536). Taking the maximum over $j$ and then applying the operator norm of $C_b^{-1}$ gives
   $$\begin{aligned}
   \|M_F^{-1}c\|_\infty&\le A_b(\eta)\|c\|_\infty,\\
   \|C_b^{-1}(M_F^{-1}c)\|_E
   &\le\|C_b^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|M_F^{-1}c\|_\infty\\
   &\le\|C_b^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}A_b(\eta)\|c\|_\infty\\
   &\le K_b(\eta)\|c\|_\infty.
   \end{aligned}$$
   The argument with a coordinate $j$ is for $n>0$. When $n=0$, both vectors are zero, $A_b(\eta)=0$ and $K_b(\eta)=1$, so the conclusion is immediate. In every dimension $A_b(\eta)\ge0$ and the leading $1$ in $K_b(\eta)$ ensures positivity.

content.lean_realization_notes: The [coordinate factor](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L538-L541) and [ambient inverse constant](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L543-L546) are the displayed $A_b,K_b$; [positivity of that constant](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L548-L560) requires the same gap. [the common inverse-bound structure](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L594-L602) stores exactly a real $K$, a proof $K>0$, and the uniform inverse estimate. [the nonzero determinant criterion](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L418-L425) and [reconstruction through the inverse frame](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L434-L443) also give $C_b^{-1}M_F^{-1}T_Fx=x$, so $T_F$ is injective, as in [frame-map injectivity](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L381-L389). The functional row is [evaluation on the basis](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L268-L271); [expansion of a functional in these coordinates](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L284-L297) and [the transposed Cramer replacement](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L299-L307) justify the scalar identity used above. The [row replacement operation](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L259-L261) and [replacement determinant](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/DeterminantFrame.lean#L263-L266) keep the frame, its matrix and its evaluation map distinct.
